question: with centering as the only variable, do the three negative classes separate from the written faces on the real read keys?

criteria.C1_control_identity: with center=None the runner's own read reproduces the real addressed_read on all 154 queries of both arms: identical fast sha, top slot, top/second cosine and margin
criteria.C2_store_immutable: centering is read-time only: store_keys/store_values/store_age hashes are identical before and after every arm-B pass
criteria.C3_threshold_source: the gate threshold is the minimum top cosine of the written group in that same arm and centering; no negative label enters the value
criteria.C4_gap_sign: gap = written_floor - class_max_top_cosine per negative class, sign reported as measured; a non-positive gap is called 'not separable by this read gate'
criteria.V1_written_bytes: if centering changes the returned fast sha of any of the 22 written faces against arm A, the verdict is centering_changes_written_bytes and no gate is proposed (dominant rule)
criteria.V2_insufficient: otherwise, if all three gaps are <= 0 the verdict is centering_insufficient: the separability problem is not in the offset layer
criteria.V3_enables: otherwise, if at least two gaps are > 0 and unwritten false refusals are <= 1/66, the verdict is centering_enables_gate and a threshold interval (lower, upper] is reported
criteria.V4_interval_empty: if the V3 conditions hold but lower >= upper the verdict is centering_no_usable_interval
criteria.V5_partial: anything else is centering_partial with per-class signs reported
criteria.unchanged: no fixture, face, position, class or anchor is retuned after the first reading

verdict.reason: centering altered the returned fast bytes of written faces; rule V1 wins
